name: uniphish-byte-cnn
task: binary URL phishing classification (phishing probability in [0, 1])
description: Unicode-native, byte-level 1D-CNN from the UniPhish IEEE paper, re-implemented as a pure-NumPy forward pass so the platform needs no TensorFlow at runtime. UTF-8 byte sequence (256-token vocab, no [UNK]) truncated/zero-padded to 600, byte embedding (256x64), five parallel Conv1D branches (kernels 2..6, 128 filters each) + ReLU + global-max-pool, dense head 640->256->128->1 (sigmoid).

param_count_breakdown.note: Components sum to 377985. The paper's Table III headline of 847,425 does not match its own described components; this implementation uses the reproducible 377,985 (see docs/paper_vs_reality.md section 1).

provenance.origin: Trained with TensorFlow/Keras; weights exported to a float32 blob + JSON manifest by scripts/export_web.py for zero-dependency inference. This NumPy runtime reproduces the exact extension/model.js forward pass.
provenance.training_data: Reproducible blend of a multilingual synthesizer (6 script families, realistic phishing construction) + real public feeds: OpenPhish + URLhaus (phishing/malicious), Cisco Umbrella top-1M (benign). Balanced (~46% phishing), per-domain capped, SHA-256 deduplicated. Adversarial min-max training on Unicode homoglyph substitutions. See data/DATASHEET.md.
provenance.weights_format: float32 little-endian, C-order, concatenated per manifest.tensors

caveats: Overconfident outputs: probabilities cluster near 0 and 1. Calibrate (temperature) before using thresholds other than 0.5/0.9 in production.

The raw model may over-score long, legitimate URLs and over-rely on suspicious TLDs (TLD swap to .com is the strongest single-model evasion, ~10% detection drop). The fused UniPhish engine compensates: the rules/brand/reputation layers and log-odds fusion recover most of this, so use this model as one weighted signal, never as the sole verdict.

Source separability: benign (Umbrella bare domains) vs phishing (URLhaus full URLs) differ structurally, so headline accuracy overstates pure phishing-semantic skill (docs/paper_vs_reality.md section 2/4).

No general multilingual accuracy advantage over an ASCII-CNN was reproduced on this data; byte-level's benefit is expected to be narrow (pure homoglyph/IDN evasion), not a blanket gain (docs/paper_vs_reality.md section 2).
Trained largely on synthetic + a few real feeds; not a substitute for a production threat-intel dataset. Not a sole basis for blocking without human/secondary review.
The model only sees the URL string: it cannot resolve shorteners (bit.ly/...) without an upstream redirect-follow.
license_note: Defensive/educational reference implementation. No malicious infrastructure is built; synthetic phishing strings are for training/testing only.
